statusVocabulary.implemented-unverified: Code written and reviewed, but never executed. Makes no claim of working.
statusVocabulary.verified: Covered by a passing automated test that exercises the stage named.
statusVocabulary.partial: Works for a stated subset; the limitation is recorded in `limitations`.
statusVocabulary.n/a: Not applicable at this stage for this capability.

framing.note: Under this architecture, LaTeX syntax support is not an application feature — TeX Live 2026 parses and typesets the document, so the parser/semantic/layout stages for LaTeX constructs are the engine's, not ours. Enumerating a few hundred LaTeX commands as 'supported' here would restate TeX's own capabilities while hiding the only things that are genuinely ours to get right: whether the engine is reachable, whether the project is mounted correctly, whether the artifact is displayed and exported faithfully, and which package sets actually resolve.
soWhatIsTracked: Engine capabilities we invoke and must configure correctly.
Application capabilities: mounting, display, export, synchronisation, diagnostics.
Package-set availability, which bounds which documents can compile at all.
The draft outline's coverage, which is explicitly non-authoritative.
framing.honesty: A capability is `verified` only where a named automated test exercises the stage. As of 2026-10-11 the suite passes (tsc clean, 93 unit/fuzz, 3 e2e) — see docs/project-state.json verificationStatus.

acmart and sn-jnl: KNOWN FAILING to compile in practical time (not in the provisioned set; every dependency fetched individually from the remote endpoint; preview did not appear within 300s). They are now tagged resolution:'remote-heavy' and selecting them raises an explicit UI notice (formatResolutionNotice) so the user is told what to expect instead of the document silently hanging. Tracked as test.fixme in remote-packages.spec.ts. Treat as not reliably working until a document actually compiles.

capabilities.capability: Instant HTML skim of the source
limitations: Built on 232 chained regex passes (C12): brace-unaware macro arguments, comment stripping ahead of verbatim stashing, non-recursive \input, non-greedy body extraction.
Makes no claim about line breaking, spacing, pagination or typography — by design.
Runs on the main thread (C13).
